title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python
summary: Al Sweigart's free book on scripting files, spreadsheets, browsers, and everyday tasks.
description: A practical introduction to automation with Python. Chapters cover file paths, regex, spreadsheets, PDFs, email, web scraping, and GUI automation, with projects you can adapt to your own chores.

title: Python argparse
summary: The standard-library guide to building command-line interfaces and argument parsers.
description: Argparse handles positional arguments, options, subcommands, defaults, and help text without third-party dependencies. The docs include a gentle tutorial and a complete API reference.

title: Python pathlib
summary: The modern, object-oriented way to work with filesystem paths in Python.
description: Pathlib replaces string-based path handling with path objects that support joining, globbing, reading, writing, and platform-aware behaviour. Essential for portable scripts and file automation.

title: PyAutoGUI
summary: Cross-platform GUI automation for mouse, keyboard, screenshots, and simple bots.
description: PyAutoGUI can move the mouse, click, type, take screenshots, and locate images on screen. The docs include safety notes and practical examples for repetitive desktop tasks.

title: Schedule
summary: A small, readable scheduler for running Python functions at intervals or fixed times.
description: Schedule provides a human-friendly API for jobs such as every ten minutes or every Monday at 09:00. It is intentionally simple and works well inside long-running scripts and small services.

title: Requests
summary: The friendly HTTP library for scripting APIs, downloads, sessions, and auth.
description: Requests is the default choice for straightforward HTTP work in Python: query parameters, JSON, headers, sessions, timeouts, and authentication. The docs are concise and example-led.
